clue.text: Pollution in the gorge sounds deliberate

parts.note: a defile is a narrow gorge or mountain pass

indicators.note: sounds says the following word's synonym is to be heard, then written as it sounds

parts.note: something deliberate is meant, done on purpose

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the dumping of rubbish in a ravine looks intentional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a verb, to stuff oneself, but it is the narrow pass; 'sounds' means a sound-alike of the synonym, not the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiling something is fouling or tainting it, so the act or state of being defiled is a kind of contamination.

clue.text: Adepts at fingerprints

definitions.meaning: a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an expert, and in British police slang dabs are the prints taken from fingers.

clue.text: Fellow applying cement to the grooves

definitions.note: the answer is a mass noun for a set of grooves

parts.note: lute is a clay cement for sealing joints, so luting is applying it

explanation.surface: A workman sets about cementing the grooves in a surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints, so luting is applying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluting is the decoration of parallel channels cut into a column or glass, a series of furrows.

clue.text: Stout garment, offering protective covering of the spine, say? .

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, the sound standing for different spelling

parts.note: a lumbar jacket would be a protective wrap for the lower back

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a sturdy coat that also supports your back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals sound: LUMBAR (of the lower spine) JACKET sounds like the woodsman's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick checked woollen coat worn by forestry workers is a heavy, robust piece of clothing.

clue.text: Marine has to transmit one sign in the opposite direction

indicators.note: in the opposite direction means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to transmit is to emit
I is the Roman numeral one
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A soldier at sea must signal backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the opposite direction' reverses EMIT I RAM as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine and maritime both describe things relating to the sea or shipping.

clue.text: Wanted twin boys to support first-born

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means coming underneath the earlier piece

parts.note: née or né means born; the masculine form NE comes first

indicators.note: twin means the same piece appears twice

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, so the twin boys are two Eds

explanation.surface: A family wished for twin sons to back up the eldest child.
explanation.walkthrough: NE is the French 'né', born; 'to support' puts the two EDs below it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed, as in a thing required or wanted, is a synonym of desired.

clue.text: State obstruction to an alliance

indicators.note: State is read as the verb, to say out loud, so the next word's synonym is spoken

parts.note: an obstruction is a block

explanation.surface: A political story: a government blocking a treaty between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country or a government, but it is the verb: say BLOCK aloud and you hear the political grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties united by a common interest, a formal coalition.

clue.text: Scope for the footloose?

parts.note: scope means space, and footloose taken literally means having feet free to move

explanation.definitionFit: Space in a car or plane seat for stretching the lower limbs.

clue.text: Behave patronisingly to Dane in conversation

definitions.meaning: to treat someone with superior, talking-down manners
said aloud, Dane sounds like deign, which means to stoop to doing something

explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop graciously, the sense the spoken Dane gives, and to talk down to someone is the other meaning.

clue.text: Unlawful killing by athlete causing great outcry

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman or woman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
murder is the unlawful killing of a person

explanation.surface: A newspaper story: a sports star kills someone and the public is outraged.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge University sportsperson, a British convention; 'by' just puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream blue murder is to make a loud, excessive protest, so the phrase stands for a huge clamour.

clue.text: The conflict in Samson Agonistes

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the title that follows

explanation.surface: A literary remark about the struggle at the heart of Milton's verse drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Samson Agonistes is Milton's drama; its title literally means Samson the contender, so the word sits in the title and fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek drama an agon is the formal contest or debate between two characters, a struggle.

clue.text: Mah-jongg as played at College?

parts.note: mah-jongg is a tile game built around a wall of tiles; College here means Eton College

explanation.definitionFit: This rugby-like game is played only at Eton College, against a brick barrier.

clue.text: Iron about four or a little later

indicators.note: about means the symbol for iron goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the ironing to be done around four o'clock or a little after.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's 'four': the time a little later than four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with the clock in mind, the hour after four is just a short while later.

clue.text: The majority used to be for pontoon

definitions.meaning: the age of majority, when one legally became an adult in Britain, was this until it was lowered to eighteen in 1970
pontoon is the British name for the card game also called blackjack or vingt-et-un

explanation.definitionFit: The old legal age of adulthood and the card game where you aim for a hand totalling that number share one name.

clue.text: Pin-up of uncovered tart

definitions.meaning: photographs of scantily clad attractive people
an open flan of soft cheese on a biscuit base

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for glamour photographs, and also an open dessert with no pastry lid.

clue.text: Severe reprimand you have to try to get over

definitions.meaning: British slang: to be due for this is to face a serious telling-off or punishment

definitions.text: you have to try to get over
definitions.meaning: the athletics event where competitors attempt to clear a raised bar

explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'be for the high jump' means facing harsh punishment, and the athletics event is literally a bar to clear.

clue.text: No. Irishman is heard to be so sententious

indicators.note: is heard says the words before it are spoken aloud

parts.note: No. is short for number, here read as the word no; Mick is a stock (now offensive) nickname for an Irishman

explanation.surface: An Irishman who answers only no is thought to be pompously moralising.
explanation.walkthrough: Say NO MICK aloud and you hear the adjective; the silent G is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic writing is full of short maxims, so it is aphoristic and pithy in a moralising way.

clue.text: Get sore at cruel English butcher

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack about, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a vicious English butcher is causing someone pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like a noun but is the verb; it rearranges AT CRUEL into ULCERAT, and E (English) ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ulcerate is to develop an open lesion, becoming raw and painful.

clue.text: Cause an artificial impression

definitions.meaning: to ... a change is to bring it about
a special ..., or doing something for ..., creates an illusion

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to bring about; as a noun it is the contrived impression made on an audience.

clue.text: A touching flirtation that needs a little 7

definitions.text: A touching flirtation that needs a little 7

parts.words: A touching flirtation that needs a little 7
parts.note: 7 points to the answer at 7 down, space to stretch the lower limbs, which this under-the-table game requires

explanation.definitionFit: Lovers nudge each other's feet under the table in this flirtatious game.

clue.text: German shepherd living in France

definitions.meaning: the breed of dog once usually called this in Britain
a native of Alsace, a region of eastern France

explanation.definitionFit: The dog breed's British name comes from Alsace, and a person from that French region shares the name.

clue.text: Gatecrasher has driven round a diversion

indicators.note: round means the reworked letters go around the single letter
a diversion sends things off their usual course, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A party gatecrasher drove the long way round a road diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' rearranges DRIVEN into INVDER, and 'round' wraps that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forces their way into a place uninvited is an intruder.

clue.text: Capital city — or the big smoke.

explanation.definitionFit: Cuba's capital gives its name to the island's cigars, a hefty thing to smoke.

clue.text: Note one extra form of excuse

indicators.note: form of says the words are reshaped into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A teacher's memo asks for an extra note as a formal excuse for absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ONE EXTRA into EXONERAT, and the note E goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free from blame, which is what excusing someone means in the sense of pardoning.

clue.text: Be positive

definitions.meaning: to be is to exist or have life
an electrical wire carrying current, as opposed to earth or neutral

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to exist, and the adjective describes a charged, current-carrying wire.

clue.text: Harris's foxy relation

parts.note: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus tales, with their dialect title for brother, as in Fox

explanation.definitionFit: In Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories this dialect word for brother is the title of the Fox and the Rabbit.

clue.text: A small orchestra appears In addition

parts.note: LSO, the London Symphony Orchestra, shortened to its initials

explanation.surface: A concert notice: a chamber orchestra will play as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' is not about the band's size but says its name is shortened: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means too or as well, adding something further.

clue.text: Fiery spirit, George Augustus — he turned Communist

parts.note: George Augustus Sala was a Victorian journalist
he refers to a man

indicators.note: turned says the word for a Communist is read backwards

parts.note: a Communist is a Red

explanation.surface: A story of a hot-headed Victorian gentleman who switched to Communism.
explanation.walkthrough: George Augustus Sala (1828-95) was a famous Victorian journalist; 'turned' reverses RED to give DER.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend this lizard-like creature lived in fire, and alchemists named the elemental spirit of fire after it.

clue.text: Introduction to ecological study in the garden

indicators.note: Introduction to picks the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A course outline: the first lesson in ecology is held out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like academic work, but it is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this is the garden where Adam and Eve lived, the archetypal paradise garden.

clue.text: Malicious gossip about Pooh left in a tree perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters gathered may be arranged in another way

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: Someone spreads spiteful stories about Winnie-the-Pooh being abandoned up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh is A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh; 'perhaps' rearranges the ten letters of the bear, the L and A TREE, the 'in' of the surface only joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carries stories about others, spreading rumours and secrets, is a spiteful gossip.
